story.head: The Blues shut down the dangerous stuff, the Islanders don’t
paras: The Islanders (10-6-5) lost 4-3 in overtime to Winnipeg on Thursday, while the Blues have won two in a row. Going in, the Blues are seventh in the Central (18th in the NHL) and the Isles fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for 15th).
The Blues’ record (.545) is about what their chances are worth. The Islanders’ record (.595) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.492), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Blues ice the puck less than anyone (1st), keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and take a lot of high-quality shots (3rd). As for the Islanders, they get their defensemen shooting (1st), roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st) and have had some of the best goaltending in the league (1st). The Blues keep dangerous shots away, but the Islanders give up a lot of them.

Robert Thomas (4 G / 16 A / 20 P in 22 GP) leads the Blues in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jimmy Snuggerud (12 G / 5 A / 17 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (9 G / 15 A / 24 P in 21 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Bo Horvat (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 21 GP) is next in line.
Joel Hofer (9-6-1 / .923 SV% in 16 GS) has been a rock in net for St. Louis and will likely start. Ilya Sorokin (8-4-2 / .918 SV% in 14 GS) has been terrific for the Islanders and will likely start.
